title: Manoj Muntashir Calls Adipurush Dialogues His 'Biggest Mistake,' Seeks Forgiveness
excerpt: The lyricist and dialogue writer expressed deep remorse over his work on the 2023 mythological drama, calling it the biggest regret of his career in a candid podcast interview.
body:
• Lyricist Manoj Muntashir described writing the dialogues for Adipurush as the "biggest mistake" of his life and said he feels "deeply ashamed" of them.
  • Speaking on the Times Now podcast Baatein Dil Se, Muntashir sought public forgiveness and admitted that defending the film after the backlash made things worse.
  • The 2023 film, starring Prabhas and directed by Om Raut, faced severe criticism over its dialogue, VFX, and portrayal of characters from the Ramayana.
  • Adipurush was produced on a budget of approximately ₹600 crore but is widely considered a commercial and critical failure.

Lyricist and dialogue writer Manoj Muntashir has publicly expressed deep remorse over his work on Adipurush, calling the 2023 mythological drama the biggest mistake of his career. In a candid interview on Times Now's podcast Baatein Dil Se, Muntashir apologised for the controversial dialogues that triggered widespread outrage after the film's release.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=oERCJ7elqQI

"Adipurush was the biggest mistake of my life. Defending that film was an even bigger mistake," Muntashir said. "Whatever happened around the film because of me, I am ashamed of all of it. With folded hands, I seek forgiveness from the people of this country."

A Film That Became a Cultural Flashpoint

Directed by Om Raut and starring Prabhas as Lord Rama, Kriti Sanon as Sita, and Saif Ali Khan as Ravana, Adipurush was released on June 16, 2023. The film had been one of the most anticipated Indian productions of its year, billed as a grand cinematic retelling of the Ramayana with a reported budget of approximately ₹600 crore.

https://x.com/dna/status/2080927281510486526

Within days of its release, however, the film became a lightning rod for criticism. Several dialogues — including now-infamous lines such as "Marega bete," "Bua ka bagicha hain kya," and "Jalegi tere baap ki" — were condemned as crude and disrespectful to the source material. Audiences and religious groups argued the language was unfit for a story rooted in one of Hinduism's most sacred texts, according to Bollywood Hungama.

The backlash was severe enough that the filmmakers were forced to revise several dialogues after release, an unusual step that underscored the scale of public anger.

'I Don't Know What I Was Thinking'

"Now when I look back, I am ashamed that I wrote them. I don't know what state of mind I was in when I wrote those dialogues."

— Manoj Muntashir, lyricist and dialogue writer

Muntashir revealed that his wife had warned him against publicly defending the film, sensing the backlash that was building even before the release. He acknowledged he should have listened. "In the beginning, I was a bit dismissive. It took me two days to understand," he told Times Now, as reported by Zoom TV.

The writer also expressed regret at not doing justice to the characters of Lord Rama and Lord Hanuman, while clarifying that some of his earlier public remarks — particularly those about Lord Hanuman — had been taken out of context. He nonetheless accepted full responsibility for the quality of the dialogues.

"The country does not forgive arrogance or dishonesty," Muntashir said. "I no longer want to be associated with either."

The Financial and Reputational Fallout

Despite generating initial box-office momentum, Adipurush grossed approximately ₹390 crore worldwide — a significant underperformance against its ₹500-600 crore production and marketing costs. Produced by T-Series and Retrophiles, the film is widely regarded as one of Bollywood's most high-profile commercial failures in recent years.

Beyond the financial hit, the controversy dealt lasting reputational damage to several people associated with the project. Director Om Raut spoke in a 2025 interview about the emotional toll the backlash took on him and his family. Saif Ali Khan later remarked that "there are certain areas like religion that you need to stay away from."

A Cautionary Tale for Big-Budget Epics

Muntashir's apology arrives at a moment when Bollywood is once again attempting to adapt Hindu epics for the big screen. Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor, is among the most closely watched upcoming productions. The Adipurush debacle has set a clear precedent: audiences expect reverence and care when filmmakers adapt sacred narratives, and missteps carry enormous consequences.

For Muntashir, who has built a reputation as one of Hindi cinema's most prominent lyricists with work on films like Tanhaji and the Border 2 album, this public reckoning marks a rare moment of unguarded vulnerability. Whether the apology reshapes public perception remains to be seen, but his acknowledgment that the criticism was justified suggests a writer grappling seriously with the weight of cultural responsibility.
nri_angle: The Adipurush controversy reignited global debates within the diaspora about Bollywood's handling of Hindu epics and cultural responsibility in big-budget filmmaking.
